terms.gloss: so long as one may live, there is hope
evidence: Ter. Heaut. 981: Modo liceat vīvere, est spēs.

terms.gloss: while there is breath, there is hope
evidence: Cic. Att. 9.10.3: ut aegrōtō, dum anima est, spēs esse dīcitur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Cicero quotes it as a saying about the sick, in indirect speech: dum anima est, spēs esse dīcitur. The direct form given here is ours.

phrases.english: So long as I’m allowed to live, there’s hope.

phrases.latin: ut aegrōtō, dum anima est, spēs esse dīcitur
phrases.english: as a sick man is said to have hope while he has breath

sources: Lewis & Short: spes
